title: Nareshwar Nath Bhargava v. State of U.P. and Others
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta, Acting Chief Justice and Hon'ble Kshitij Shailendra, J.
disposition: Petition disposed; clause 6.5 objection to be decided by speaking order.
headnote: Writ challenging the electricity bill for connection No. 4772265963 disposed. The billing dispute must be raised under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petitioner may file an objection before respondent No. 3 within two weeks, to be decided by a speaking order within four weeks thereafter.
facts: Nareshwar Nath Bhargava filed Writ-C No. 40783 of 2023 in the Allahabad High Court against the State of Uttar Pradesh and two others, challenging the electricity bill for connection No. 4772265963. After listings in November and December 2023, including a direction to place the matter before a bench of which Justice Siddhartha Varma was not a member, the petition came up on 17 January 2024. Counsel for the Electricity Department then submitted that the billing dispute had to be raised under the Supply Code.

holding_units.topic: Billing dispute relegated to a clause 6.5 objection
holding_units.holding: A challenge to an electricity bill must be raised in accordance with clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petitioner is permitted to file an objection against the bill before respondent No. 3 within two weeks, and respondent No. 3 shall decide that objection by a speaking order within the next four weeks. The writ stands disposed of on that basis.

principle_tags.application: The writ challenging the electricity bill was disposed of, the petitioner being permitted to file a clause 6.5 objection before respondent No. 3 within two weeks.
The Court accepted that the dispute over the bill for connection No. 4772265963 had to be raised under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the electricity bill for connection No. 4772265963
not_decided.note: Left to respondent No. 3, which is to decide the petitioner's objection by a speaking order.
